answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, publicly auditable tasks, with each task requiring a small stake that is forfeited if answers conflict with later checks. Tasks draw on varied sources—a shale survey, a cipher puzzle, a prism calibration—so copying one response is insufficient. This does not prove one person per agent, but makes each fake identity costly: the attacker must fund many stakes and sustain distinct, checkable work, while failures burn capital.
